newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar shoots up vs yen on weak Japan output data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar shoots up vs yen on weak Japan output data.

text.p: 0434 GMT --*Dollar jumped against yen in early afternoon Tokyo in quick reaction to surprisingly weak Japanese industrial production data for April, dealers said.
*JGBs prices rose on the data, which prompted slew of short-covering and pushed dollar as high as around 116.20 yen.

*April production fell by 0.4 percent. Economists polled had expected rises ranging from 0.3 percent to 1.5 percent. *Stop-loss dollar buying may be triggered at 116.10 yen, said a European bank dealer. "The outpout data was too weak, prompting short-covering in mark/yen as well," he added.
*Dollar facing resistance at around 116.20-30 yen, where major overseas operators sold dollars overnight.
*"Focus is on whether the dollar will be able to break through that point," said another European bank dealer.
*Japanese exporters unlikely to move to sell dollars at current level as they have already arranged forward dollars sales covering period to end-June, said a Japanese bank dealer.
*Yield of benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.650 percent at 0503 GMT, down from 2.735 percent at midday.
*Dollar rose against mark in tandem with dollar/yen's rally, staying above 1.700 marks.
0300 GMT -*Dollar eased from earlier highs against yen by Tokyo midday on Thursday due to rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) yields.
*"The dollar drifted lower against the yen as JGBs continued to be sold this morning," said a city bank trader.
*Dollar underpinned by buying interest near Wednesday's New York low of 115.28 yen, dealers said.

*"The dollar slid lower as the market failed yesterday to push it decisively above the 200-day moving average, which lies slightly below 117.00 yen. However, there seems to be buying interest at around 115.30 yen," a trust bank trader said.
